defects.exploit_shape: two concurrent submissions for the same tenant with different parameters derive different execution_ids, take different Redis locks, read the same un-decremented equity, and can both pass the ceiling

defects.remediation: ExecutionRecordRepository.claim_execution_within_capacity, called from execute_with_idempotency for live-bound orders. The only capital bound was a read-then-compare against `self.current_equity` in PROCESS MEMORY with nothing reserved, decremented or locked, and no FOR UPDATE, advisory lock or exposure table anywhere on the path; `claim_execution` guarantees one worker per GIVEN execution and says nothing about two DIFFERENT ones. Because generate_execution_id folds quantity and price into the canonical string, two orders differing in either took different execution ids AND different Redis locks, cleared the identical ceiling independently, and both proceeded. The fix makes the claim and the capacity decision ONE transaction serialised per tenant by pg_advisory_xact_lock, summing admitted notional from execution_records. THE RESERVATION IS THE `EXECUTING` ROW - no new table and no second piece of state that can leak if the process dies between writing it and claiming. Only EXECUTING rows are summed: counting PENDING intents made two recorded intents block each other permanently, which two of the new tests caught. A declared paper/backtest engine keeps the original claim. The per-order ceiling is unchanged and still runs.
defects.remediation_evidence: tests/test_trade01_concurrent_exposure_postgres.py (28 tests, local PostgreSQL, multi-connection). THE DEFECT IS DEMONSTRATED AS A PASSING TEST: test_without_the_reservation_two_rows_both_reach_executing races the ORIGINAL claim_execution from two separate connections and asserts the database ends up holding 120% of the account's fundable notional in EXECUTING rows. Then: two connections released by a threading.Barrier admit exactly one; ten concurrent attempts at 25% of the ceiling admit exactly four; refusal leaks no capacity; FAILED releases it; COMPLETED never holds it; a one-hour-old EXECUTING row is released while a one-second-old one is NOT (negative control); idempotency holds sequentially and under a five-connection race; the advisory lock is released on both the success and the refusal path, asserted from pg_locks; one tenant cannot block another. The live-order path is never enabled - the exchange stub raises on any call. tests/regression/baseline/live_order_path.json re-recorded through the sanctioned _baseline_note process; the collaborator sequence changes by exactly one entry in the same position.

API-05.resolution: ROOT CAUSE: _get_openapi_url() consulted NO environment variable at all and no task definition sets ENABLE_OPENAPI, so production hid /docs and /redoc (correctly, after ENV-05) and PUBLISHED the schema those pages are rendered from - the hiding and the publishing withheld and disclosed the same surface. POLICY DETERMINED: /docs and /redoc are the INTERACTIVE, browser-executable consoles; /openapi.json is the MACHINE-READABLE SCHEMA they render from. Both now follow runtime_env.local_state_is_acceptable(), with ENABLE_DOCS and ENABLE_OPENAPI as INDEPENDENT explicit overrides consulted first in both directions - 'publish the schema for a machine consumer but keep the browser console off' is a legitimate configuration and has to be expressible. DOCUMENTATION IS NOT DISABLED EVERYWHERE: development and test environments, and any machine saying DEV_MODE=true, serve all three exactly as before. WHY IT WAS SAFE TO CHANGE NOW, when the earlier pass declined: NOTHING in this repository fetches /openapi.json over HTTP - the frontend mentions it only in comments, no CI workflow references it, and tests/test_route_contract.py reads app.openapi() IN PROCESS. CloudFront EEOXECPHQ8SR0 does carry an explicit /openapi.json cache behaviour and two middlewares list the path as public, but those are ROUTING and AUTH facts that PREDATE the ENV-05 change: they exist because /docs used to be served in production and had to be reachable unauthenticated for the page to work. Once the console became local-only the schema's publication lost its reason. The CDN behaviour and the allowlists are LEFT IN PLACE and now forward to a 404, because deleting a deployed cache behaviour is an infrastructure change and a routed path that answers 404 is harmless. ENABLE_OPENAPI=true restores the previous behaviour with one variable.

CONN-01.resolution: A CREDENTIAL ROTATION NOW TAKES EFFECT IN-PROCESS. Before: the exchange connection pool keys on sha256([user_id, exchange_id]) and omits the credential (correct for the pool primitive -- it still separates users and venues), but `store_keys` (the POST /api/exchange/keys create-OR-ROTATE handler) did not evict the pooled client on a rotation, so a client built from the OLD keys kept being served until the connection was deleted or the process restarted. `delete_connection` already evicted for this reason; the rotation path did not. FIX: `store_keys` now calls `release_exchange(user_id, exchange_id)` AFTER the vault write succeeds, popping and closing the stale pooled client so the next `get_or_create_exchange` reconstructs with the fresh credential. Placed after the persist (a failed store never evicts a good client) and a no-op on a first-time connection. The pool key is deliberately unchanged -- the fix evicts around the primitive rather than re-keying it. Independently re-verified: staging/verify_phase10_open_findings.py -> CONN-01 REMEDIATED (store_keys calls release_exchange).

ENV-01.resolution: ROOT CAUSE: test_connection_pooling_safety had NO mocking. get_or_create_exchange('user_123','binance','key1','secret1') constructs a real ccxt.pro.binance and ConnectionEngine.connect() awaits load_markets(), which for a CREDENTIALED binance client issues GET https://api.binance.com/sapi/v1/capital/config/getall with X-MBX-APIKEY: key1. So the unit lane made an outbound AUTHENTICATED request to a live production venue using a credential invented in the test body, and was red either way: with network AuthenticationError -2008 'Invalid Api-Key ID.', without network ExchangeNotAvailable. Neither outcome says anything about pooling. FIX: the boundary is now named. (1) CONNECTION-POOLING CORRECTNESS - sha256 key, dict, asyncio.Lock, pop+close on release - is pure in-process bookkeeping, fully decidable here, and IS tested. (2) VENUE AUTHENTICATION/CONNECTIVITY is a statement about a third party and a secret, is not decidable in the unit lane, and is NOT tested and NOT claimed. The real get_or_create_exchange, the real ConnectionEngine.connect() and the real release_exchange all run; only the venue CLIENT CLASS is replaced, by a controlled in-process transport that receives the same assembled config dict (so which credentials reached which client is OBSERVABLE) and answers load_markets() locally. Nothing skipped, xfailed, credentialed or weakened; the assertions are STRONGER than the originals, which only compared object identity - identity alone cannot distinguish 'isolated correctly' from 'both users got the same wrong client'.

ENV-03.resolution: TWO defects under one id, both closed. (a) core/config.py called a bare load_dotenv(); with no argument that calls find_dotenv(), which walks up from the CALLING MODULE's directory - backend_app/ - so it resolves backend_app/.env and NEVER reaches the repository-root .env. Proven by this engagement's own record: Phase 6's CORRECTION-006 added ENV=development to the ROOT .env, recorded it as applied, and it was INERT. (b) Every credential gate was spelled 'if not value:' and bool('YOUR_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY') is True, so the seven placeholders in backend_app/.env satisfied validate_required(), validate_config() and the vault's own 'if not keys_string:'. The sharpest instance is .env.example's STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_live_your-stripe-secret-key: billing._validate_keys accepts a Stripe key ONLY when it starts with sk_live_, written precisely so a test-mode key cannot grant a paid entitlement - and the placeholder starts with sk_live_. A prefix is not a credential either. FIX: new core/secret_validation.py with FOUR verdicts - MISSING / EMPTY / PLACEHOLDER / USABLE. EMPTY is kept distinct from MISSING on purpose: an empty value in a deployed environment is a secret-manager reference that resolved to nothing, a broken deployment wearing the costume of an unconfigured one. USABLE is deliberately the WEAK claim - the module recognises fakes and cannot verify a credential against its provider, and says so. ONE VOCABULARY: Settings.WEAK_JWT_SECRET_PATTERNS now POINTS AT the shared list instead of keeping a second copy (two lists for one concept is how detect_ml_nodes ended up with two spellings and a gate that missed half of them). TWO TIERS chosen from the code that already refuses, not a wish list: 6 REQUIRED_DEPLOYED_CREDENTIALS where MISSING, EMPTY and PLACEHOLDER are all fatal, and 7 PLACEHOLDER_REJECTED_CREDENTIALS where MISSING is accepted. Settings.assert_credentials_are_production_grade() is called from main.lifespan BEFORE any port is bound; production FAILS CLOSED and an unset ENV counts as DEPLOYED. Development keeps its documented behaviour and keeps it VISIBLE - print_config_status() prints each unfit variable and its verdict with '(local environment - reported, not fatal)' beside them. KILL-01.resolution: NEW IN PHASE 8, AND MORE SERIOUS THAN THE FINDING THAT LED TO IT. GlobalKillSwitch._redis_get caught every exception and returned None, so None meant BOTH 'Redis answered and the key is not set' AND 'Redis could not be read'. Two consequences, opposite in direction, same root cause. (1) FAIL-OPEN: the fail-closed `except` at the bottom of is_active() was UNREACHABLE for a connection error - control fell through to `if value is None: return False`, so a Redis outage reported the kill switch as NOT ACTIVE and a TRIGGERED switch stopped blocking the moment Redis went away, directly contradicting the module's own documented fail-closed policy. It was broader than an outage: `redis_manager` is a `__getattr__` proxy that raises AttributeError when never initialised, so any worker that had not brought Redis up also read 'switch off'. (2) PERMANENT LOCKOUT: once latched, recovery lifted the latch only `if probe_result is not None`, and a healthy system's resting state IS None - so a recovered Redis with no key could never lift it, contradicting the same docstring's promise that transient failures do not deadlock the platform. Fixed by introducing `RedisUnavailable`, raising it from _redis_get, failing closed on it in is_active(), and deciding recovery on whether Redis ANSWERED rather than on whether the key had a value.

LIB-04.resolution: NEW, AND INTRODUCED BY THE LIB-01 REPAIR ITSELF. Narrowing this module's broad `except Exception` handlers to `except _PostgrestAPIError` was the right direction - a broad handler had been relabelling an AttributeError from a None client as 'Failed to look up library entry.', a statement about a row that was not the problem - and it meant ANY failure that is not a PostgREST APIError escaped the handler entirely and reached the application's generic 500. Not theoretical: supabase-py performs the request with httpx, so the commonest real read failure (DNS, TLS, connection reset, read timeout) arrives as httpx.ConnectError / httpx.ReadTimeout / httpx.RemoteProtocolError, none of which is an APIError. The narrowing turned 'the database was unreachable' from a retryable 503 into a 500. FOUND BY THE POSTGRESQL LANE of the full regression, not by reading the code: eleven failures across four files, all 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR on POST /api/library/{id}/clone or DELETE /api/library/{id}, including the two test_validation_sweep cells this phase had just turned green. The escaping exception was psycopg2.InterfaceError: connection already closed - a dead client left reachable by a save/restore race on a module global across two threads in tests/test_lib01_clone_strategy_postgres.py (a TEST defect, fixed with a threading.local; see staging/REGRESSION_ORDER_ISOLATION.md). What it REVEALED is not a test defect. FIX: `_read_did_not_complete(operation, exc)` as a second handler at every client call on both paths - logs the exception TYPE with exc_info=True, so a programming error stays fully visible to an operator (which the original broad handler was not, logging only f'...: {exc}' with no traceback), and raises the same MarketplaceError(MARKETPLACE_READ_FAILED) -> 503. The _PostgrestAPIError handler stays FIRST at every site, because when the database answers its answer is the diagnosis. Two sites stay best-effort and swallow (the clone_count increment and the verified-clone rating marker): the clone row already exists and is owned by the caller, so failing the request would report a failure for an operation that succeeded.

PAPER-02.resolution: ROOT CAUSE: paper_trading_service.place_order's MARKET branch called _insert_and_accept - an INSERT at CREATED then an UPDATE to ACCEPTED - BEFORE any funding decision. There was no affordability check on the market path at all: avail_bal was read and used ONLY in the limit branch. The shortfall therefore surfaced downstream inside paper_accounting.apply_fill as InvariantViolation('available_balance'), answered 500 PAPER_INVARIANT_VIOLATION, leaving order_state=ACCEPTED / legacy_status=OPEN / filled_quantity=0 / rejection_reason=NULL for ever. FIX: the funds gate sits BETWEEN the INSERT and the ACCEPT - not before the insert (Requirement 16.6 wants the rejection PERSISTED as an order carrying its reason, and a row never written carries nothing) and not after the accept (the order would already have been in a state it could fill from). CREATED->REJECTED is one of Requirement 16.2's nine transitions and is already seeded in paper_order_allowed_transitions, so NO new order model, state or migration. Threshold is the existing accounting.required_funds() = money(notional * (1 + fee_rate + slippage_rate)), which is Requirement 16.6's formula; reason is the existing REJECTION_INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS; refusal is the existing PaperInsufficientFunds -> 400. NO LOCK AND NO ATOMIC RESERVATION WERE ADDED: apply_fill asserts every invariant before its first statement and repo.bump_version carries the account version as a predicate, so two racing workers can never both move the balance. What was missing was never the money - it was the losing order's state. A lock would also contradict Requirement 16.6's 'SHALL lock no funds'. THE FILL-FIRST WRITE ORDER WAS NOT REORDERED: the fill row is a documented idempotency anchor ('money moved before the fill row exists could be applied twice'), pinned by test_a_conflicting_retry_resumes_the_fill_row_rather_than_writing_a_second_one and tests/property/test_paper_confluence.py. Reordering would have traded a reporting defect for a double-spend window. WHAT WAS MOVED is the POSITION write, to match paper_simulator.apply_fill's canonical fill->money->ledger->position order; the divergent fill->position->money->ledger order orphaned a POSITION on a version conflict - a phantom holding breaking the equity identity. Aligned, not invented. Also: fill_event_id made deterministic (exec_paper_<order_id>) so uq_paper_fill_event can deduplicate; _execute_fill split into a retry wrapper plus _attempt_fill with RESUME semantics; _assert_account_unmoved before the first write; 409 now carries phase= and partial_write=.

TRADE-10.resolution: NEW IN PHASE 8, found by building the capacity reservation on top of claim_execution's predicate. ExecutionRecordRepository.claim_execution's PostgreSQL fast path wrote `SET status = 'executing'` and matched `WHERE (status = 'PENDING' OR status = 'pending')`. execution_records.status is the enum `executionstatus`, whose labels are UPPERCASE only, so PostgreSQL cannot parse either lowercase literal as a value of that type: the statement raised `invalid input value for enum executionstatus: "pending"` on EVERY call, the except caught it, logged 'falling back', and the ORM path silently did the work. The audit recorded this atomic `UPDATE ... RETURNING` as the only atomic predicate on the live order path; it had never executed there. The outcome was still correct, because the fallback is a single guarded UPDATE, but the documented path was untested and every execution claim emitted a warning. Both halves of the statement are now uppercase and the predicate is `upper(status::text) = 'PENDING'`, which is correct whether the column is an enum or a varchar.

WORK-03.resolution: migration 025 adds bot_ownership_claims with PRIMARY KEY (user_id, symbol) - the key FleetManager._bot_key actually uses, not strategy_id. Claimed by one statement: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... WHERE heartbeat_at < now() - threshold, so PostgreSQL re-evaluates the predicate under the row lock and the loser gets ZERO ROWS rather than an exception. DO UPDATE and not DO NOTHING, because a permanent lock would strand a bot after pod death. owner_token is regenerated per claim and scopes release/heartbeat, so a reaped worker cannot release its successor's claim. Chosen over a Redis SET NX because core/cache/redis_manager.py is deliberately fail-soft, so an outage would answer 'not acquired' for everybody and a non-fail-soft refactor would answer 'acquired' for everybody: an availability dependency must not be able to flip a correctness invariant in the unsafe direction. Wired into start_bot before BotRunner is constructed and released on all FOUR exit paths. FleetManager._heartbeat_claim keeps the claim live for the bot's lifetime and surrenders the runner when ownership is lost, distinguishing 'store unreachable' (tolerated, bounded by the stale threshold) from 'ownership taken over' (immediate stop). No-claim-store policy reuses runtime_env.local_state_is_acceptable() rather than adding a second detector.

PAPER-04.detail: NEW, found while fixing PAPER-02. When _attempt_fill writes the fill row and then loses the bump_version race, the fill row exists with no money movement and no ledger entry. The retry wrapper ADOPTS that row on the next attempt - that is what the fill-first ordering is for - and across ten races the residue was 0 every time. What remains is the case where all three attempts are exhausted. The residue is then BOUNDED (one row per exhausted order), DETECTABLE (one query, _has_unsettled_fill), NON-FINANCIAL (no balance moved, no ledger entry, and no position after the write-order alignment), SELF-HEALING on retry (the deterministic fill_event_id is adopted, not duplicated) and VISIBLE on the 409 via phase='FILL' and partial_write=True. REPORTED RATHER THAN FIXED because removing it entirely means either reordering the writes - which deletes the documented idempotency anchor - or adding a compensating delete, which is a new write on a failure path and needs its own idempotency story. Measured residue: unsettled_fill_rows -> 0 in 10 of 10 races (staging/probe_paper02_race_stability.py).

PAPER-05.detail: NEW. The market path gates on accounting.required_funds() = money(notional * (1 + fee_rate + slippage_rate)), which is Requirement 16.6's formula. The LIMIT branch computes its own estimated_cost with the FEE ONLY - no slippage - so it diverges from required_funds by notional * slippage_rate. DIRECTION: the limit gate is marginally MORE PERMISSIVE than the market gate for the same notional. It is NOT a path to negative cash - apply_fill's invariants still hold at fill time - it is a path to an order being accepted and locked that the slippage-inclusive threshold would have refused. NOT CHANGED because estimated_cost is simultaneously (a) the gate threshold, (b) the amount LOCKED on the account and (c) the amount RELEASED on cancellation or fill. Raising it changes all three together across the resting-order, cancellation and fill paths, and a release that does not match its lock is a worse defect than a marginally generous gate. The correct repair is one coherent change to the resting-order lifecycle with its own tests, not a one-line edit inside a rejection fix.

SAST-01.detail: DISPOSITION ESTABLISHED IN PHASE 6: FALSE POSITIVE AT REPOSITORY SCOPE, plus a real SCOPE DEFECT IN THE CONTROL. Owners: the SAST gate (scope) and the local migration's author. (a) The file is not in the repository - git status reports '??', git ls-files does not list it, git log for the path is empty - and the gate discovers modules with BACKEND_APP.rglob('*.py'), a filesystem walk with no git awareness, so CI on a fresh checkout has nothing to flag. TRADE-06.detail: CARRIED FORWARD, STILL OPEN, with one part of it closed in Phase 7. safety_config.validate_safety_config_integrity() has ZERO call sites - nothing in the application, the entrypoints or CI invokes it, so it has never run - and its live-trading branch compares VYOMQUANT_MODE / AERORA_MODE against "live_trading", which is the SystemMode ENUM value and not a value either variable ever holds (the trading modes are safe / paper / live). So even if it were wired, that branch could not fire. WHAT PHASE 7 CHANGED: its PRODUCTION_ROUTER_ENABLED assertion is removed. That assertion raised in production unless the execution router was ENABLED - the opposite of what the feature_flags docstring, .env.example and all four shipped task definitions say - so had this function ever been called it would have refused to boot every deployment this repository ships. WHAT PHASE 7 DELIBERATELY DID NOT DO: wire it up. Wiring a validator whose central comparison cannot fire would convert a dead control into a control that reports success without having checked anything, which is worse than a documented absence. Its docstring now records that it is uncalled, and a test pins the code-and-note pair so the two cannot drift apart silently. The same shape was then found a second time in config.validate_production_config - see DEADVALIDATOR-02.

TRADE-08.detail: CARRIED FORWARD, STILL OPEN, NOT RE-MEASURED IN PHASE 7. Retry idempotency is TIME-BOXED by a 5-minute bucket: generate_execution_id derives the key from (tenant, strategy, symbol, BUCKETED TIMESTAMP, side, qty, price) with execution_interval_minutes defaulting to 5, so a retry landing in a later bucket produces a different execution_id, hence a different clientOrderId, hence a NEW order at the venue - sidestepping both the database dedupe and the venue's own dedupe. An idempotency key that changes with the clock is not an idempotency key.

corrections.withdrawn_claim: Two invariants asserted by my own PAPER-01 test oracle.
corrections.what_was_wrong: (1) The oracle summed unrounded position values and rounded once; the engine quantizes each position independently. (2) The oracle asserted equity == capital + realized_pnl - fees as an identity. It is not one: measured 100008.48 against 100008.49, because cash is derived from quantized position VALUES while realized_pnl quantizes independently, so the two quantizations do not compose.
corrections.corrected_to: The false identity was DROPPED, not hidden behind a tolerance, and replaced with the invariant the implementation does guarantee exactly: per fill, equity falls by exactly that fill's fee, valuing the position at that fill's price on both sides.
corrections.lesson: An audit that silently adjusts its own oracle to match the code has stopped measuring anything. Both errors were mine and both were found by the tests failing, which is the oracle doing its job.

corrections.what: My own PAPER-02 test oracle asserted a post-fill balance of capital - required_funds and expected 49.92. The ledger held 49.93.
